news.title: Rozetka accelerated the restructuring of its business model to reduce self-managed retail sales and transition toward a decentralized network of smaller fulfillment hubs.
Commercial property owners in Ukraine have begun refusing to rent warehouse spaces to Rozetka due to risks of missile strikes.
Rozetka submitted proposals to Ukrainian authorities for post-strike tax deferrals and relief, which were rejected by the Ministry of Finance.

pains.hypothesis: Rozetka faces substantial operational margin pressure and logistics overhead as it transitions from a centralized distribution hub to dispersed smaller fulfillment centers.
The company is exposed to delivery delays and inventory bottlenecks due to commercial property owners refusing to lease warehouse space to the retailer.
Rozetka's liquidity is constrained by having to absorb billions of hryvnias in uninsured physical losses without specialized state tax deferrals or interest-free relief.
Rozetka must shift reliance from direct inventory retailing to marketplace commissions to mitigate the financial risk of holding inventory in centralized facilities.
